en.title: Number of Fleet Options with Two-Wheelers and Four-Wheelers
en.description:
Each query gives a total number of wheels; form a fleet from unlimited two-wheeled and four-wheeled vehicles. Two options are different only if the number of vehicles of some type differs; arrangements are not counted.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n values of wheels; 1≤n≤100000, 1≤wheels[i]≤1000000.
en.output: Output n lines with the number of options, in input order.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2 / 0 / 2; 0 / 1 / 0; 3 / 3 / 4. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Odd totals are impossible; for an even total, the number of four-wheelers ranges from 0 to w//4, and each such count uniquely determines the number of two-wheelers.
